steps.text: Combine flour, white sugar, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a small bowl.
In a large bowl, mash bananas. Mix in eggs, milk, and margarine until smooth. Stir in flour mixture.

Heat 1/2 inch oil in a deep fryer or heavy-bottomed pan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Working in batches, carefully drop batter by spoonfuls into hot oil; cook, turning once with slotted spoon, until golden brown, 2 to 8 minutes, depending on size. Drain on paper towels and dust with confectioners’ sugar.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Banana Fritters
raw_recipe.description: These easy banana fritters made with ripe bananas are dipped in batter seasoned with cinnamon and nutmeg. They’re a nice alternative to apple fritters.

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a recipe for banana fritters b/c my husband grew up on them. His family is Haitian and this is a traditional thing they make. I couldn't use his mother's recipe b/c her measurements were not exact. It was a little bit of this and a little bit of that. I thought this was a good recipe, but I would add more sugar to the batter. My husband and I both agree that it needed more bananas. I think that if you like it for a desert, more sugar would be appropriate. It also depends how much you like bananas. We like the taste of bananas to be very strong and noticable. Also, I tried a previous suggestion and piped it out of a bag. The oil was way too hot and they came out like burned funnel cakes. After the first attempt, I used less heat and transfered the batter to a bowl and used a 1/3 measuring cup as my spoon. The looked just like his moms. With more sugar and more banana, I would make this a five star recipe! (I also only use overripe bananas so avoid having to throw them out. They also seem to be more sweet.)

I was looking for something different to make besides banana bread and thought this recipe would be a nice change. I substituted the white flour for brown rice flour, used coconut oil for frying (didn't deep fry), used butter instead of margarine and, since I didn't have baking powder, I used 1/4 tsp. baking soda plus 1 tsp. vinegar to replace the missing ingredient. They came out like little silver dollar pancakes! Very tasty. I liked them with and w/o the powdered sugar.

very yummy. my son gobbles them up. I handed one to my husband and he said that he doesn't like bananas, then proceeded to eat half the plate. my favorite part are the little itty bitty ones. I have made them per the recipe and have made them with added peaches. the ones with peaches added were the best, I think apples would probably work just as well. others have complained that they are too doughie. they can be. it is best to make them small, spread the batter when addind to the oil or squish in the middle half way thru frying.

I gave five stars because of the changes I made to the recipe. Instead of 2 bananas I used 3 bananas, i used 3 tablespoons of milk, 3 1/2 tablespoons of sugar, 2 teaspoons of vanilla and 1 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon. As someone else mentioned I too used lower heat. With these changes it was absolutely delicious.

It was fine and the texture was just right, but I used nowhere near 1 quart of oil and the banana flavor was barely detectable as Chevonne said. Based on that and other people's comments of blandness, I upped the cinnamon to 1 tsp. and added an extra banana. Wonderful. Beyond that, just some tips: a) A piping bag isn't really necessary. The trick is to drop the right amount of batter in the oil all at once, otherwise you get these strings and odd shapes. I used on overfilled gravy ladle and let a dollop drop in. b) Eggs and milk should be room temp or you risk having a browned outside but uncooked middle. c) Use a lower temp. All stoves are different, so do a test batch at 325 first, then adjust. I ended up using 275 to avoid browning too fast and cooking everything in the middle. d) Don't overcrowd the pan. Each fritter lowers the oil temp, and it's much easier to manage five or six than 10. e) Don't add sugar to the batter, otherwise they'll brown faster. I also used tongs to flip and remove them from the pan before sprinkling with powdered sugar. Great recipe!

Great pancake batter! I followed the recipe word for word, minus the sugar for dusting, and instead of deep frying the batter, I made delicious banana pancakes! I also left tiny little chunks of banana in the batter. It made 12 pancakes, cooking 4 at a time on a flat skillet. They are so flavorful, I just ate them plain with my hands while standing up and cooking/cleaning up. They would be a good food to easily pack up for kids or adults to eat on the go.
it was excellent. I used a cookie scoop to drop the balls into the oil and they came out looking similar to hushpuppies. 2 bananas were enough for our taste but i did increase the sugar.

An easy and straightforward recipe. I made a batch with 1ripe banana plus 1ripe plantain, (which had been cut into slices and fried; leftovers from the other day). The plantain added an extra caramalized depth, but was a little more difficult to mash up. I also added 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and doubled the cinnamon/nutmeg. For anyone having trouble with the outside burning before the inside cooks; make your balls smaller. I was scooping ~tablespoon, which puffed up to three bite fritters. Cooked 4-5 minutes each, they were quite dark, edging on almost burnt, yet full cooked inside. Next time I will do smaller, teaspoon sized scoops, which should cook in 2-3 and not be so dark.

Easy and delicious...I added two tbsp more sugar two more bananas and 1/2 cup of shreaded cocoanut after trying the recipe the way it was originally written but the ingredients were all things we keep on hand and my whole family loves them as a weekend breakfast treat

We used all spice instead of nutmeg (we didn't have any in the house), we also used vanilla instead of milk (also because we had not gone grocery shopping). We dusted the fritters with sugar on all sides then put on cooling rack. They were great! Some also drizzled chocolate on the fritters which gave it more flavor.

Yum! being vegan i sub'd a few things. milk- soymilk, eggs- egg replacer, margarine- earth balance. being health conscious (i know it's deep fried! just saying) AP flour- WW flour, sugar- agave syrup. used maybe 2 Tbs of powdered sugar sifted over. if you have overripe bananas and are tired of banana bread try these. they are super addicting... youve been warned.
I had two really ripe bananas. Found this recipe that was easy. Next time, I’ll make it I’ll be a little more careful of the oil temperature. Delicious highly recommended.

No doubt about it, they are delicious and easy to make. I just ran into one problem, I heated the oil to the recommended temperature and they turned golden brown very quickly. My problem is, the insides were not cooked. I just put them in the oven for 7 minutes and they were perfect. Next time I will lower the temperature on the oil. I just don't want to believe that there are 916 calories in each one. Please tell me that I am mistaken.
I used canola oil instead of margarine and it still taste good. I dusted it with a combination of powdered milk and sugar and it made it more delicious.
They where so delicious.my family really enjoyed them.I recommend this recipe to everyone

This recipe was easy to make. Not the best looking fritters but tasty. I popped them in the oven after dusting. Long enough to warm them. I think I need to get the batter slightly thicker and add some crunch to it.
Absolutely delicious.

By mashing the bananas and dropping by the spoonful cannot have the same effect that your illustration shows. One needs to keep the bananas in a whole condition but cuts into sections then coated in the flour to turn out like your illustration.
Great recipe. Family loved it
I made this with no sugar or sweeteners, no egg(I used vegan egg replacer powder) as well as just frying (not deep frying as the recipe says) and even though it stuck to the pan, it tasted very good.
